Prediction-Error Criteria and a Structural Term's Own Parameters

Source: R/order.R
assert_criterion_reach.Rd

Raises an error naming the penalty and the remedy when aic(), bic() or cv() would have to select a hyperparameter of a penalty over the own parameters of a structural term: the group departures of a score-driven filter over a panel, or a covariance class that reaches into one.

Usage

assert_criterion_reach(
  spec,
  design,
  method,
  reach = c("all", "smooth", "kinked")
)

Arguments

spec

A StatmodSpec().

design

The design.

method

An OuterMethod(), or NULL.

reach

Which penalties the criterion selects: "all", "smooth" or "kinked".

Value

NULL, invisibly. The function is called for the error.

Details

A prediction-error criterion reads the effective degrees of freedom, and their derivative, over the coefficients alone, where such a penalty covers nothing. The exact gradient of aic() there is zero, so a search would stop at its first evaluation and report convergence. cv() and the path along which a kinked penalty is swept are built on the same blocks. reml() and ml() span the term's parameters in their determinant and estimate a twice differentiable penalty there. A penalty with a kink there has no criterion that can select its hyperparameter. The hyperparameter can be held by writing its value in the term, for example lasso(~id, lambda = 2), and the penalty is then fitted over the term's own parameters by a proximal route, without a criterion.

Which penalties a criterion reaches depends on its role, and only those are checked: an outer_criterion reaches the smooth penalties, and the kinked ones as well when no sparse_criterion is given, while a sparse_criterion reaches only the kinked ones.

See also

assert_criterion_order(), structural_penalized()

Examples

dd <- data.frame(x = runif(60))
dd$y <- rnorm(60, dd$x)
spec <- statmodels7:::statmod_spec(y ~ x, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(),
                                   dd)
statmodels7:::assert_criterion_reach(spec, statmodels7:::statmod_design(spec),
                                     aic())
